frequency_source: OPUS OpenSubtitles v2024 Swahili frequencies https://object.pouta.csc.fi/OPUS-OpenSubtitles/v2024/freq/sw.freq.gz , with news-genre support from OPUS GlobalVoices v2018q4 https://object.pouta.csc.fi/OPUS-GlobalVoices/v2018q4/freq/sw.freq.gz (FrequencyWords 2018 has no sw file).
how_to_tell_apart: Swahili does not overlap in everyday pronouns and politeness with the other Latin-script languages in this task: mimi, wewe, hapana, ndiyo, asante, tafadhali, habari, kwaheri, kesho, wapi, nini and daktari are sufficient. Bantu noun-class prefixes (m-, wa-, ki-, vi-, u-) are an extra structural cue. The OpenSubtitles list contains many proper names from a dubbed series (for example court-title names); those were discarded when choosing common_words. Short syllables such as na, ya and ni also occur in other languages with other meanings and should not be used alone.
test_said: Ofisini pa kata ninaomba cheti cha makazi ili nikiwasilishe kazini.
Dawa nilizoachiwa baada ya kliniki zimeisha na ninauliza kama ninaweza kupata dawa tena.
Mzigo niliotuma kwa basi ulipaswa kufika jana na bado sijapata taarifa.
Kitanda kilicholetwa kina mguu uliopasuka na nataka kibadilishwe.
Zahanati ya mtaa ninataka kupima kikohozi kilichokaa wiki mbili.
Chanjo ya surua kwa mtoto inapatikana lini wiki hii katika kituo chenu?
Sihitaji bima mpya kutokana na simu hii wala sitatoa taarifa binafsi.
Ofa ya kifurushi cha simu hainivutii kwa sababu nimebadilisha mpango mwezi uliopita.
uncertain: Regional vocabulary differs between Kenya and Tanzania (pesa/hela, some greetings); the list follows forms that rank in both OpenSubtitles and GlobalVoices.
karibu is a greeting or invitation in Swahili and also an ordinary word in some other languages, so it is only useful with other Swahili function words.
